market_question: Will the US acquire part of Greenland in 2026?
reasoning: Territorial acquisition by peaceful agreement or force is exceedingly rare. Despite historical US interest, there is no ongoing negotiation, and Denmark and Greenland remain firmly opposed. The 2-year deadline makes a binding agreement or use of force improbable.
evidence_points: No US territorial acquisition of foreign land since 1947.
Denmark and Greenland have consistently and strongly rejected any sale or transfer.
The resolution requires a binding agreement or de facto control via force, neither of which appears plausible by end‑2026.
sources_consulted: Historical record of US territorial changes
Current geopolitical assessments of Arctic sovereignty
